questions.question: A branch client asks for office.microsoft.com. A local DNS entry exists in a non-authoritative matching zone. What should FortiGate do?

choices.text: Return the locally configured address without upstream lookup.
choices.feedback: Correct. A matching zone can answer from its local DNS entry; the non-authoritative setting permits fallback when no local answer exists.

choices.text: Forward the query to the central resolver first.
choices.feedback: That would bypass the configured local answer and defeat the local-resolution path.

choices.text: Drop the query because the zone is non-authoritative.
choices.feedback: Non-authoritative does not mean deny. It permits upstream resolution when a local record is absent.

choices.text: Rewrite the query to the client's original resolver.
choices.feedback: The proxy decides from the configured zone and entry; it does not rewrite the client to a different resolver.

questions.question: The local A record works, but another name in the same zone never reaches the branch resolver. Which setting is the first check?

choices.text: DNS database authoritative state and forwarder.
choices.feedback: Check that the zone is non-authoritative when fallback is intended and that its forwarder is configured and reachable.

choices.text: Firewall session TTL and TCP half-close timer.
choices.feedback: DNS queries are normally UDP or TCP transactions; session TTL is not the zone-forwarding decision.

choices.text: SD-WAN service rule source-address match.
choices.feedback: SD-WAN may affect the route to the forwarder, but it does not select the DNS database's zone-specific forwarder.

choices.text: Local-in policy logging on the ingress interface.
choices.feedback: Local-in policies govern traffic to FortiGate services, not the proxy-policy path that applies this feature.

questions.question: A DNS database is configured and referenced by a DNS filter profile, but no query is intercepted. What policy property is required?

choices.text: Policy must use central NAT mode.
choices.feedback: Central NAT is unrelated to the inspection-mode requirement for transparent conditional DNS forwarding.

choices.text: Policy must use proxy inspection mode.
choices.feedback: Proxy-based firewall policy inspection is the documented requirement; flow-based inspection does not invoke this feature.

choices.text: Policy must enable session pickup.
choices.feedback: Session pickup affects HA session synchronization, not whether the DNS proxy applies the conditional database.

choices.text: Policy must reference a virtual IP.
choices.feedback: A VIP is not required for this DNS interception path.

questions.question: Which platform constraint can make an otherwise correct transparent conditional DNS configuration unsupported?

choices.text: FortiGate has only one VDOM.
choices.feedback: VDOM count is not the documented limitation; the feature can be configured in the relevant VDOM context.

choices.text: DNS forwarder is reachable over IPsec.
choices.feedback: VPN reachability is supported when routing and source addressing are correct.

choices.text: Client uses an IPv6 resolver address.
choices.feedback: IPv6 forwarder and source-address settings are documented for conditional forwarding.

choices.text: Model has 2 GB RAM or less.
choices.feedback: Correct. Fortinet excludes models with 2 GB RAM or less from this proxy-related feature.

questions.question: Two administrators edit different rules in one package. Which mechanism allows the first administrator to lock only one rule?

choices.text: Enable Workspace mode and Per-Policy Lock.
choices.feedback: Correct. Workspace mode with Per-Policy Lock allows a single policy to be owned without locking the entire package.

choices.text: Enable Workflow Mode and approval sequencing.
choices.feedback: Workflow Mode provides approval transactions; it is not the granular policy-edit lock described here.

choices.text: Lock the complete ADOM before every edit.
choices.feedback: An ADOM lock is broader than necessary and prevents unrelated work.

choices.text: Clone the package into a second ADOM.
choices.feedback: Cloning creates a separate configuration copy rather than coordinating concurrent edits to the same policy.

questions.question: An administrator cannot individually lock a policy that is referenced by a Policy Block. What is the supported interpretation?

choices.text: The ADOM database has become read-only.
choices.feedback: Read-only database state is not implied by this restriction.

choices.text: The policy package must be upgraded first.
choices.feedback: Policy package version is not the stated reason that the lock is unavailable.

choices.text: The Policy Block membership prevents individual locking.
choices.feedback: Correct. The guide explicitly excludes policies used by Policy Blocks from individual policy locking.

choices.text: The FortiGate has rejected the pending installation.
choices.feedback: This is a FortiManager workspace restriction, not a device installation rejection.

questions.question: A policy shows a red padlock and the tooltip names another administrator. What does that prove?

choices.text: The policy failed syntax validation during install.
choices.feedback: A lock color is an ownership indicator, not an installation-validation result.

choices.text: An ADOM-wide lock is held by the device.
choices.feedback: An ADOM-wide lock is a different lock scope from the individual policy indicator.

choices.text: Another administrator currently owns that policy lock.
choices.feedback: Correct. Red indicates another administrator's lock; the tooltip exposes owner and time.

choices.text: The policy has been installed to every target.
choices.feedback: A lock does not prove that any installation has occurred.

questions.question: A change inserts three policies and other administrators cannot add rules. Which lock is likely active?

choices.text: The selected policy's object-reference lock.
choices.feedback: Object references do not serialize insertion and reordering of multiple rules.

choices.text: The policy block's installation-target lock.
choices.feedback: Policy Block target scope is not the documented sequence-lock behavior.

choices.text: The global ADOM database migration lock.
choices.feedback: Database migration is not indicated by a package-level sequence-lock banner.

choices.text: The policy-sequence lock protecting rule order.
choices.feedback: Correct. Adding or reordering multiple policies creates a sequence lock that protects ordering.

questions.topic: Cloud archive offload with Storage Fabric Connectors
questions.question: FortiAnalyzer has a valid cloud connector but the upload feature cannot be enabled. Which prerequisite should be checked first?

choices.text: Storage Connector Service license validity.
choices.feedback: Correct. Fortinet requires a valid Storage Connector Service license before cloud log upload can be enabled.

choices.text: FortiGate ADOM device-count threshold.
choices.feedback: ADOM device count is not the entitlement for cloud storage upload.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer event-handler suppression timer.
choices.feedback: Event-handler suppression affects event generation, not the storage connector service entitlement.

choices.text: FortiGate OFTP log encryption algorithm.
choices.feedback: OFTP encryption is a different device-to-Analyzer log transport mechanism.

questions.topic: Cloud archive offload with Storage Fabric Connectors
questions.question: S3 upload fails during TLS negotiation while credentials and bucket permissions are correct. What dependency is missing?

choices.text: A second FortiAnalyzer in collector mode.
choices.feedback: Collector mode is not required for the storage connector's TLS trust relationship.

choices.text: AWS region-specific event handler mapping.
choices.feedback: Event-handler mapping does not participate in the TLS handshake to object storage.

choices.text: The cloud provider CA certificate chain.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiAnalyzer requires the cloud provider CA certificates to be imported before uploading to S3, Azure Blob or Google.

choices.text: A local SQL dataset for archive logs.
choices.feedback: A SQL dataset is not the certificate trust dependency for object upload.

questions.topic: Cloud archive offload with Storage Fabric Connectors
questions.question: Where is the remote bucket or container path bound to the storage connector?

choices.text: FortiSoC event-handler rule settings page.
choices.feedback: Event handlers evaluate Analytics logs and do not define cloud object destinations.

choices.text: Device Manager log-fetch schedule page.
choices.feedback: Log Fetch schedules retrieve logs from another Analyzer; they do not configure cloud upload.

choices.text: Advanced Device Log Settings page.
choices.feedback: Correct. Device Log Settings enables upload, selects the Fabric Connector and accepts the remote path.

choices.text: FortiGate Security Fabric authorization page.
choices.feedback: FortiGate authorization is unrelated to FortiAnalyzer's cloud storage destination.

questions.topic: Cloud archive offload with Storage Fabric Connectors
questions.question: An object appears in the cloud bucket. What can the engineer safely conclude?

choices.text: All Analytics SQL queries now run in S3.
choices.feedback: Cloud object upload does not move the Analytics SQL query engine into object storage.

choices.text: Local archive retention is automatically disabled by upload.
choices.feedback: The upload setting does not by itself disable local retention.

choices.text: Every log is searchable through FortiView in cloud.
choices.feedback: An object in a bucket does not prove that FortiView can query it as local Analytics data.

choices.text: The configured upload path transferred an object successfully.
choices.feedback: Correct. Provider-side object evidence confirms transfer, but not Analytics indexing or restore semantics.

questions.question: A FortiSwitch image uploads successfully but the controller reports failed signature validation. What should happen next?

choices.text: Stop the upgrade and verify the official image.
choices.feedback: Correct. A signature warning is a trust-gate failure; verify model, release and official image before installation.

choices.text: Retry installation until the warning disappears.
choices.feedback: Repeated retries do not resolve an invalid signature or unsupported image.

choices.text: Disable FortiLink and flash the same file.
choices.feedback: Disabling FortiLink does not make an unverified image trustworthy.

choices.text: Assume transfer success proves image authenticity.
choices.feedback: File transfer and image authenticity are separate stages.

questions.question: A switch logs Unverified Image Detected, and its BIOS lacks signature-verification support. What does this evidence indicate?

choices.text: The switch has lost its FortiLink controller.
choices.feedback: Controller reachability is a separate state from the image-verification warning.

choices.text: The BIOS capability limits image verification.
choices.feedback: Correct. Fortinet documents a warning when the BIOS does not support image-signature verification.

choices.text: The image has already passed dual-signature validation.
choices.feedback: The warning is not evidence that the image passed verification.

choices.text: The switch has exhausted its PoE budget.
choices.feedback: PoE allocation does not explain the firmware integrity warning.

questions.question: Which evidence is needed before concluding that signature verification should be available on a model?

choices.text: The current MAC table and VLAN database.
choices.feedback: MAC and VLAN state do not establish firmware verification support.

choices.text: The number of active FortiLink ports.
choices.feedback: Port count is not the documented model/BIOS capability check.

choices.text: The model feature matrix and BIOS capability.
choices.feedback: Correct. The model feature matrix and BIOS support determine whether image verification is available.

choices.text: The switch's LLDP neighbor and PoE status.
choices.feedback: LLDP and PoE telemetry do not establish the firmware verification capability.

questions.question: The controller reports that the firmware file reached the switch. What remains unproven?

choices.text: The image was copied to local storage.
choices.feedback: Transfer evidence can support that the image reached storage, but it is not a trust result.

choices.text: The FortiLink transport carried the file.
choices.feedback: Successful transport proves file movement, not signature validity.

choices.text: The switch recognized the target model.
choices.feedback: Model recognition may be checked separately and is not implied by transfer alone.

choices.text: The image signature was accepted as trusted.
choices.feedback: Correct. Signature verification is a separate pre-installation integrity and trust check.

questions.question: The MLD diagnostic reports num_links=3 and link IDs for 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz. What does this establish?

choices.text: The client negotiated three active MLO links.
choices.feedback: Correct. The MLD output's link count and link IDs are direct evidence of multi-link association.

choices.text: The AP is using three separate SSIDs.
choices.feedback: Multiple links can belong to one logical MLD/SSID rather than three separate SSIDs.

choices.text: The client roamed between three controllers.
choices.feedback: MLD link identifiers are not controller-roaming records.

choices.text: The VAP has three independent RADIUS servers.
choices.feedback: RADIUS server count is unrelated to the negotiated MLD link count.

questions.question: A WPA3-SAE MLO VAP is configured, but association does not negotiate MLO. Which security prerequisite matters?

choices.text: Enable WPA2 transition mode on every radio.
choices.feedback: WPA2 transition mode is not the documented MLO security prerequisite.

choices.text: Enable SAE H2E-only for WPA3-SAE.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiOS enables SAE H2E-only with WPA3-SAE for the supported MLO configuration.

choices.text: Disable PMF to permit legacy clients.
choices.feedback: Disabling PMF is not the required MLO security setting and weakens management-frame protection.

choices.text: Use an open SSID with captive portal.
choices.feedback: An open captive portal does not satisfy the documented WPA3 MLO security mode.

questions.question: An FAP-443K shows MLO on 5 and 6 GHz but not 2.4 GHz. What is the likely explanation?

choices.text: The controller has disabled every 2.4-GHz radio.
choices.feedback: Do not infer a controller fault before checking model capability.

choices.text: The client must use three separate VAP profiles.
choices.feedback: Separate VAP profiles are not required to explain the documented radio limitation.

choices.text: The model's 2.4-GHz radio does not support MLO.
choices.feedback: Correct. FAP-441K and FAP-443K support MLO on 5/6 GHz, not their 2.4-GHz radio.

choices.text: The 2.4-GHz band requires a separate RADIUS realm.
choices.feedback: RADIUS realm selection does not create hardware MLO capability.

questions.question: A standalone MLO AP must continue authenticating clients without its FortiGate controller. Which configuration model is required?

choices.text: Tunnel-mode VAP with controller-only authentication path.
choices.feedback: Controller-dependent tunnel authentication does not satisfy the standalone requirement.

choices.text: Proxy ARP with central RADIUS accounting enabled.
choices.feedback: Proxy ARP and accounting do not provide local AP authentication.

choices.text: Mesh root role with CAPWAP discovery enabled.
choices.feedback: Mesh root role and CAPWAP discovery are separate wireless functions.

choices.text: Bridge mode with local standalone and local authentication.
choices.feedback: Correct. The guide requires bridge mode and local standalone, bridging and authentication settings.

questions.question: FortiNAC reports that an SMS provider accepted a notification, but the handset never receives it. Which boundary is next?

choices.text: Inspect provider message status and carrier delivery.
choices.feedback: Correct. Provider acceptance is not carrier delivery; inspect the provider message ID and downstream delivery status.

choices.text: Rebuild the FortiNAC LDAP sponsor mapping.
choices.feedback: LDAP sponsor mapping is separate from an already accepted SMS transaction.

choices.text: Change the RADIUS dynamic VLAN attribute.
choices.feedback: RADIUS VLAN attributes do not control SMS carrier delivery.

choices.text: Disable the HTTPS SMS connector and retry mail.
choices.feedback: Changing delivery channels without checking provider status can create duplicates and hide the real boundary.

questions.question: A guest sponsor is missing from the sponsor workflow, but the SMS connector test succeeds. What should be inspected?

choices.text: Twilio message throughput and carrier route.
choices.feedback: Provider throughput does not determine whether a user is recognized as an eligible sponsor.

choices.text: The sponsor's LDAP group mapping and membership.
choices.feedback: Correct. Sponsor eligibility is driven by LDAP group mapping, separate from SMS delivery.

choices.text: The FortiNAC proxy inspection mode.
choices.feedback: Proxy inspection mode is unrelated to sponsor identity mapping.

choices.text: The DNS database authoritative flag.
choices.feedback: DNS zone authority does not control LDAP group membership.

questions.question: The connector cannot reach the SMS provider hostname. Which evidence best isolates the failure?

choices.text: FortiNAC endpoint's RADIUS Access-Accept.
choices.feedback: RADIUS authentication proves endpoint access, not provider connectivity.

choices.text: The guest's sponsor group membership.
choices.feedback: LDAP membership may affect sponsor eligibility but not HTTPS reachability.

choices.text: Outbound DNS/TLS and provider HTTP response.
choices.feedback: Correct. DNS, TLS and HTTP response evidence distinguish transport, trust and provider rejection.

choices.text: The FortiNAC event-handler correlation rule.
choices.feedback: Event correlation does not establish that the SMS provider endpoint is reachable.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the FortiNAC 9.4 SMS change?

choices.text: Only carrier email-to-SMS remains supported.
choices.feedback: The 9.4 feature summary says API/HTTPS support was added alongside the prior method.

choices.text: SMS is now delivered through RADIUS CoA.
choices.feedback: RADIUS CoA is an endpoint enforcement mechanism, not the SMS transport.

choices.text: FortiNAC replaces LDAP with SMS identity.
choices.feedback: SMS delivery does not replace directory identity or sponsor mapping.

choices.text: API/HTTPS gateway integration supplements Mail-to-SMS.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC 9.4 adds API/HTTPS provider integration, including Twilio.

questions.question: FortiNAC-F can read FortiSwitch MAC tables but VLAN changes fail after an OS upgrade. Which plane is most relevant?

choices.text: SNMPv3 trap receiver and polling interval.
choices.feedback: SNMP may support visibility and traps, but the documented FortiLink VLAN control path uses REST API.

choices.text: REST API token scope and OS-specific transport.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiLink VLAN control uses the REST API token; the other credential planes have separate duties.

choices.text: RADIUS shared secret and EAP method.
choices.feedback: RADIUS handles endpoint authentication, not FortiGate management API VLAN writes.

choices.text: SSH host-key trust and CLI command timeout.
choices.feedback: CLI is required for discovery, but REST API token is the VLAN control mechanism.

questions.question: After adding the REST API token, managed FortiSwitches disappear from Network Inventory. Which credential should be restored first?

choices.text: FortiGate System Administrator SSH/CLI account credentials.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC-F still requires the System Administrator CLI account for managed FortiSwitch discovery.

choices.text: Endpoint RADIUS user password.
choices.feedback: Endpoint RADIUS credentials do not discover managed FortiSwitch objects.

choices.text: REST API token Trusted Host restriction.
choices.feedback: The token may be valid for API operations, but it does not replace CLI discovery.

choices.text: Switch SNMPv3 trap destination and polling.
choices.feedback: SNMP supports monitoring and notifications, but the integration guide specifically requires CLI credentials for managed-switch discovery.

questions.question: An API token is configured, but switch monitoring and traps stop arriving. Which protocol was incorrectly removed?

choices.text: RADIUS for endpoint EAP authentication.
choices.feedback: RADIUS is separate endpoint authentication, not the SNMP monitoring plane.

choices.text: REST API for VLAN control operations.
choices.feedback: REST API does not replace SNMP trap and monitoring functions.

choices.text: SNMPv3 for monitoring and notifications.
choices.feedback: Correct. SNMPv3 continues to supply monitoring, visibility and traps.

choices.text: SSH/CLI for switch discovery.
choices.feedback: CLI remains required for discovery, but the symptom specifically identifies missing SNMP functions.

questions.question: A runbook recommends enabling rest-api-key-url-query on FortiOS 8.0. What is the correct response?

choices.text: Enable it globally before adding the token.
choices.feedback: The historical workaround is not valid on FortiOS 8.0.

choices.text: Use it only on the FortiLink interface.
choices.feedback: The interface scope does not restore a command removed from the release.

choices.text: Replace the token with an SNMPv3 user.
choices.feedback: SNMPv3 cannot replace REST API VLAN control.

choices.text: Do not use it; FortiOS 8.0 removed it.
choices.feedback: Correct. The updated Community article states that FortiOS 8.0 removes the command and query-parameter method.

questions.question: A RADIUS Access-Accept returns the expected dynamic VLAN, but FortiNAC cannot poll FortiSwitch inventory. What should be checked?

choices.text: REST API, CLI and SNMP management credentials.
choices.feedback: Correct. Successful endpoint authentication does not prove the independent FortiGate management channels work.

choices.text: Only the endpoint's certificate CN value.
choices.feedback: Certificate CN mapping is an endpoint identity control, not FortiSwitch inventory polling.

choices.text: Only the FortiAP's WPA3 SAE H2E setting.
choices.feedback: WPA3 security does not control FortiNAC's FortiLink inventory management.

choices.text: Only the guest sponsor LDAP group mapping.
choices.feedback: Sponsor mapping does not participate in FortiSwitch polling.

questions.topic: Intune SCEP and Entra ID EAP-TLS
questions.question: The InTune challenge-password option is missing from a SCEP enrollment request. What prerequisite is most likely absent?

choices.text: A FortiGate SD-WAN Underlay license is enabled.
choices.feedback: SD-WAN licensing is unrelated to SCEP challenge generation.

choices.text: An Azure Directory OAuth server with Tenant ID.
choices.feedback: Correct. The Intune option requires an Azure Directory OAuth server with a non-empty Tenant ID.

choices.text: A FortiNAC sponsor LDAP group is configured.
choices.feedback: Sponsor LDAP groups do not provide the OAuth connection used for Intune SCEP.

choices.text: A FortiPAM browser extension is installed locally.
choices.feedback: FortiPAM's browser extension has no role in certificate enrollment.

questions.topic: Intune SCEP and Entra ID EAP-TLS
questions.question: SCEP issuance succeeds, but EAP-TLS authenticates the certificate without returning the expected group attributes. Which mapping is missing?

choices.text: DNS database zone to forwarder mapping.
choices.feedback: DNS forwarding does not authorize RADIUS users.

choices.text: FortiGate API token to switch model mapping.
choices.feedback: FortiGate API tokens manage network devices, not FAC SAML groups.

choices.text: Remote SAML user/group bindings and RADIUS attributes.
choices.feedback: Correct. Certificate issuance is separate from remote SAML identity binding and group-sourced RADIUS attributes.

choices.text: FortiPAM secret target to launcher mapping.
choices.feedback: FortiPAM launcher mappings do not affect RADIUS authorization.

questions.topic: Intune SCEP and Entra ID EAP-TLS
questions.question: Which deployment is explicitly unsupported for the FortiAuthenticator Intune SCEP enrollment option?

choices.text: Azure commercial tenant with a valid Tenant ID.
choices.feedback: Azure commercial tenants are the documented target when the OAuth server is configured correctly.

choices.text: Local CA with a valid current certificate.
choices.feedback: A valid local CA is a required enrollment dependency.

choices.text: RADIUS policy using a SAML realm.
choices.feedback: SAML realm support is part of the documented RADIUS integration.

choices.text: Azure Government GCC, GCC High or GCC DoD.
choices.feedback: Correct. The enrollment guide excludes Azure Government GCC, GCC High and GCC DoD tenants.

questions.topic: Intune SCEP and Entra ID EAP-TLS
questions.question: A SCEP request remains unavailable to clients even though the request object exists. Which service boundary should be checked?

choices.text: SCEP service and interface HTTP access.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiAuthenticator requires SCEP enabled and HTTP access enabled on interfaces serving SCEP clients.

choices.text: FortiGate switch-controller image signature mode.
choices.feedback: Firmware signature verification does not expose the SCEP endpoint.

choices.text: FortiManager policy sequence lock ownership.
choices.feedback: Policy sequence locks are unrelated to SCEP availability.

choices.text: FortiSIEM AWS region list.
choices.feedback: AWS region configuration has no bearing on the SCEP listener.

questions.question: Which launcher can use FortiPAM 1.9 agentless mode according to the documented list?

choices.text: Native SSH client with local terminal forwarding.
choices.feedback: Native launchers are not part of the agentless web-launcher list.

choices.text: Web Browsing launcher with full browser proxy.
choices.feedback: Web Browsing is explicitly excluded from agentless mode.

choices.text: Web SSH launched through supported Chrome or Edge.
choices.feedback: Correct. Web SSH is supported in agentless mode with Chrome or Edge.

choices.text: Firefox Web RDP launcher with agentless mode.
choices.feedback: Firefox is not supported for agentless mode.

questions.question: A user ends an agentless session and expects the recording to upload. Which action completes the documented lifecycle?

choices.text: Close the target's SSH daemon process.
choices.feedback: Target SSH process termination is not the browser recording lifecycle control.

choices.text: Select Stop sharing in the browser header.
choices.feedback: Correct. Stop sharing closes the session and uploads the recording.

choices.text: Delete the secret after disconnecting.
choices.feedback: Deleting the secret is unnecessary and destructive.

choices.text: Wait for the FortiClient agent heartbeat.
choices.feedback: Agentless mode does not require FortiClient.

questions.question: The user can launch a secret in Firefox but cannot use agentless mode there. What is the likely explanation?

choices.text: Firefox requires a RADIUS realm for tab sharing.
choices.feedback: RADIUS realms do not enable browser tab sharing.

choices.text: Firefox supports agentless only for native launchers.
choices.feedback: Agentless mode is not a native-launcher mode.

choices.text: Firefox needs a different FortiPAM license tier.
choices.feedback: The documented limitation is browser support, not a license tier.

choices.text: Firefox is outside the documented agentless browser support.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM 1.9 lists Chrome and Edge and explicitly excludes Firefox.

questions.question: On macOS, an agentless session opens but recording is unavailable. Which host permission is required?

choices.text: Screen and System Audio Recording for the browser.
choices.feedback: Correct. The guide requires macOS Screen & System Audio Recording permission for agentless mode.

choices.text: Full Disk Access for the FortiPAM service account.
choices.feedback: Full Disk Access is not the documented permission for tab capture.

choices.text: Network Extensions permission for FortiClient VPN.
choices.feedback: FortiClient VPN is not required by agentless mode.

choices.text: Bluetooth access for the target administrator.
choices.feedback: Bluetooth access is unrelated to browser tab recording.

questions.question: FortiSIEM receives findings from us-east-1 but not eu-west-1. What is the first AWS-side check?

choices.text: Rebuild the FortiSIEM event parser for all regions.
choices.feedback: Parser changes are premature when the service may not be enabled in the missing region.

choices.text: Enable Security Hub in eu-west-1 and list the region.
choices.feedback: Correct. Security Hub is region-scoped and each intended region must be enabled and listed.

choices.text: Change the FortiSIEM Windows Agent restart policy.
choices.feedback: Windows Agent supervision is unrelated to AWS Security Hub collection.

choices.text: Move the AWS account to a different FortiSIEM ADOM.
choices.feedback: ADOM placement does not enable Security Hub in a region.

questions.question: Which access protocol should the FortiSIEM credential use for this integration?

choices.text: AWS CloudTrail SQS long-poll receiver.
choices.feedback: CloudTrail SQS is a different AWS integration path.

choices.text: Generic HTTPS syslog with CEF framing.
choices.feedback: Syslog CEF is not the documented Security Hub SDK collection mechanism.

choices.text: AWS Security Hub SDK.
choices.feedback: Correct. FortiSIEM uses the AWS Security Hub SDK and PHP V3 SDK.

choices.text: SNMPv3 polling with context engine ID.
choices.feedback: SNMPv3 is not used to retrieve AWS Security Hub findings.

questions.question: Test Connectivity succeeds, but no findings appear in FortiSIEM. What does the test not prove?

choices.text: That the access key is syntactically valid.
choices.feedback: A successful test can support that the access key is usable.

choices.text: That FortiSIEM can reach the service endpoint.
choices.feedback: Connectivity success supports endpoint reachability and authentication.

choices.text: That the selected AWS region code is accepted.
choices.feedback: Region-code validation may be part of successful connection setup.

choices.text: That Security Hub is enabled and has regional findings.
choices.feedback: Correct. Connectivity does not prove regional service enablement or that findings exist to be collected.

questions.question: An AWS CloudTrail record shows AccessDenied for a Security Hub API call. What is the best next action?

choices.text: Identify denied action and refine the IAM policy.
choices.feedback: Correct. Use the denied action as evidence and grant only the required least-privilege permission.

choices.text: Replace the FortiSIEM parser with a custom regex.
choices.feedback: Parser changes cannot correct AWS authorization failures.

choices.text: Disable Security Hub in every AWS region.
choices.feedback: Disabling the service removes the source rather than fixing access.

choices.text: Increase the FortiSIEM event retention policy setting.
choices.feedback: Retention does not resolve an API authorization denial.

questions.topic: Inline-CASB application detection and tenant restriction
questions.question: A SaaS tenant-restriction header is absent from HTTPS requests. Which inspection mode is required?

choices.text: Certificate inspection with SNI logging only.
choices.feedback: Certificate inspection does not expose HTTP headers for insertion.

choices.text: SSL deep inspection with a trusted FortiSASE CA.
choices.feedback: Correct. Deep inspection decrypts HTTPS so Inline-CASB can inspect and modify HTTP requests.

choices.text: Passive WAN health measurement on the endpoint.
choices.feedback: Passive WAN measurement does not decrypt or alter SaaS HTTP traffic.

choices.text: DNS filtering without decrypting application traffic.
choices.feedback: DNS filtering alone cannot insert an HTTP request header.

questions.topic: Inline-CASB application detection and tenant restriction
questions.question: An application category is allowed, but one SaaS application must be blocked. Which control is designed for this exception?

choices.text: A second global DNS database zone.
choices.feedback: DNS zones control name resolution, not per-application CASB actions.

choices.text: A FortiGate local-in policy sequence.
choices.feedback: Local-in policies protect FortiGate services, not SaaS application traffic through FortiSASE.

choices.text: An Application Override for that application.
choices.feedback: Correct. Application Overrides can assign an individual application a different action than its category.

choices.text: A RADIUS reply attribute on the user.
choices.feedback: RADIUS attributes may inform identity policy but are not the documented per-app override object.

questions.topic: Inline-CASB application detection and tenant restriction
questions.question: Corporate accounts work, but personal accounts are rejected by the SaaS provider. What does the inserted header accomplish?

choices.text: It changes the endpoint's default DNS resolver.
choices.feedback: DNS resolver selection is not the tenant-restriction function.

choices.text: It assigns the user a FortiSASE device tag.
choices.feedback: Device tags are a separate posture and identity mechanism.

choices.text: It changes the TLS certificate issuer at the endpoint.
choices.feedback: TLS inspection establishes the trust path but does not itself encode tenant identity.

choices.text: It communicates the allowed workspace or organization identifiers.
choices.feedback: Correct. The provider validates the header's allowed workspace or organization identifiers.

questions.topic: Inline-CASB application detection and tenant restriction
questions.question: Where should an engineer confirm the header that Inline-CASB inserted?

choices.text: Inline-CASB log details and the Change Headers field.
choices.feedback: Correct. The documented verification uses Inline-CASB logs and the Change Headers field in log details.

choices.text: FortiGate BGP neighbor state and routing table.
choices.feedback: BGP state does not show HTTP header insertion.

choices.text: FortiPAM session video archive index view.
choices.feedback: FortiPAM video storage is unrelated to FortiSASE traffic inspection.

choices.text: FortiSwitch PoE guard-band utilization dashboard status view.
choices.feedback: PoE utilization is unrelated to SaaS HTTP request modification.

questions.question: The SD-WAN Setup Wizard is absent from the FortiGate GUI. Which condition should be verified first?

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer Storage Connector Service license.
choices.feedback: FortiAnalyzer storage licensing does not enable the FortiGate SD-WAN wizard.

choices.text: Both SD-WAN Underlay and Application Monitoring licenses.
choices.feedback: Correct. Fortinet requires both SD-WAN Underlay and Application Monitoring licenses.

choices.text: FortiNAC-F FortiLink REST API token field.
choices.feedback: FortiNAC-F API tokens do not control SD-WAN wizard visibility.

choices.text: FortiManager ADOM workspace sequence lock status.
choices.feedback: FortiManager sequence locks do not affect the FortiGate wizard.

questions.question: The wizard creates members, an SLA and a service rule, but Internet traffic still follows the old route. What is missing?

choices.text: A second SD-WAN Underlay license.
choices.feedback: The wizard's route requirement is separate from licensing once the objects are created.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch image signature check.
choices.feedback: Firmware signature validation is unrelated to IP routing.

choices.text: A default route to the SD-WAN zone.
choices.feedback: Correct. The guide explicitly requires adding the default static route after the wizard completes.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer cloud storage path.
choices.feedback: Cloud storage configuration does not change FortiGate forwarding.

questions.question: The wizard is being used for a branch with three Internet underlays. What is the documented limitation?

choices.text: The wizard supports only IPv4 gateway addresses.
choices.feedback: The guide includes IPv4 and IPv6 gateway choices.

choices.text: The wizard cannot create a Performance SLA.
choices.feedback: Performance SLA is one of the wizard's generated settings.

choices.text: The wizard requires all interfaces to be aggregate members.
choices.feedback: Aggregate membership is not a universal wizard requirement.

choices.text: The wizard supports a maximum of two interfaces.
choices.feedback: Correct. Three underlays exceed the wizard's two-interface scope.

questions.question: Two qualifying members meet the SLA. Under Lowest Cost, which setting decides the preferred member?

choices.text: The configured member cost, with lower cost preferred.
choices.feedback: Correct. Lowest Cost (SLA) uses cost to choose among qualifying members.

choices.text: The DNS database zone name in the policy.
choices.feedback: DNS zone names do not affect SD-WAN member cost.

choices.text: The FortiAP radio channel width setting.
choices.feedback: Wireless channel width is unrelated to WAN path selection.

choices.text: The FortiNAC sponsor group priority value.
choices.feedback: Sponsor group priority does not affect SD-WAN selection.

questions.question: The wizard review screen shows a healthy SLA. What additional evidence is needed before declaring the branch operational?

choices.text: A FortiPAM agentless recording upload event log.
choices.feedback: Privileged-session recording is unrelated to SD-WAN forwarding.

choices.text: A default route plus an SD-WAN test session.
choices.feedback: Correct. Verify the separate default route and then confirm a real session selects the intended member.

choices.text: A FortiSIEM AWS Security Hub CMDB record.
choices.feedback: AWS discovery does not prove FortiGate route installation.

choices.text: A FortiAuthenticator SCEP approval record entry status.
choices.feedback: SCEP enrollment is unrelated to SD-WAN route selection.
